policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere שִׂים and ketiv שום are both infinitive forms of the same verb ('to set/leave'); ASV 'will leave to my husband neither name nor remainder' renders either identically and no note is mapped to the unit. Base qere fallback retained.

Qere מֵהַרְבַּת and ketiv מהרבית are orthographic variants of the same hiphil infinitive ('from multiplying'); ASV 'destroy not any more' does not distinguish them and no note is mapped. Base qere fallback retained.

ASV prints 'the request of his servant', which is the ketiv עבדו ('his servant'); the qere עַבְדֶּךָ ('thy servant') is relegated to the mapped textual_variant note 'Another reading is, thy.' The English wording and the note together decide for the ketiv.

ASV 'go and set it on fire', addressed to Absalom's servants, is a second-person plural imperative matching the qere וְהַצִּיתוּהָ; the ketiv והוצתיה is a first-person form ('and I will set it on fire'), which the ASV wording excludes.
